decisive_items: inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis
lesion filled the foramen of Magendie, exerted mass effect on the medulla
elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal
response.rationale: R4 uniquely integrates the vermian location, foramen of Magendie involvement, and MRS findings (elevated choline, reduced NAA) that are characteristic of medulloblastoma. R2 lacks the specific vermian localization and MRS evidence. R5 is contradicted by the absence of hemorrhage/calcification on GRE T2* and lacks DWI/MRS support. C1 is an incomplete append-only variant of R4, duplicating only the vermian span without the full diagnostic picture.

rejected.why: Support spans are generic (cerebellar syndrome, T2 hyperintensity) and do not capture the vermian location, foramen of Magendie involvement, or MRS findings that are decisive for medulloblastoma.
Directly contradicted by the raw span 'GRE T2* sequences showed no hemorrhage or calcification', which is atypical for hemangioblastoma; also lacks DWI and MRS evidence.
Redundant append-only completion of R4, providing only the vermian localization without the additional decisive features already present in R4.
